title: Mark Sanchez to plead guilty in case connected to Indianapolis altercation
author: James Boyd
content:
Former NFL quarterback and broadcaster Mark Sanchez has filed a motion to plead guilty in the case connected to an altercation in downtown Indianapolis last October in which he was stabbed, according to online court records.

Sanchez filed the motion Thursday in Marion County (Ind.) Superior Court, although it’s unclear what charges he is pleading guilty to. The motion also requested a sentencing hearing, which court documents indicate could be on either Nov. 9 or Nov. 16, and a judge must agree to the plea deal.

Sanchez was charged with one felony count of battery resulting in bodily injury, plus misdemeanor charges of unauthorized entry of a motor vehicle, public intoxication endangering the life of another and battery resulting in bodily injury. A jury trial was scheduled to begin Tuesday.

Nick Sanchez Jr., the former Fox broadcaster’s legal advisor and older brother, called the filing a “positive development” in a statement released to The Athletic.

“We are finalizing an agreement with the prosecutor’s office that provides a path toward resolving the state’s case,” Sanchez Jr.’s statement read. “We’re also encouraged by the constructive conversations taking place regarding the related civil matter. There is real momentum toward bringing this entire chapter to a close.”

Sanchez, 39, was in Indianapolis to work a game between the Indianapolis Colts and Las Vegas Raiders for Fox the weekend of the altercation. He attended practice the Friday before the game but never called the game because of the incident involving 69-year-old truck driver Perry Tole that led to Sanchez’s stabbing and hospitalization.

Tole filed a lawsuit against Sanchez and Fox Corporation a day after Sanchez was criminally charged, seeking damages and demanding a jury trial. Fox parted ways with Sanchez roughly a month later, and he was replaced by former New Orleans Saints quarterback Drew Brees.

“We are pleased with the constructive and professional conversations we’ve had with Mr. Sanchez’s team,” Matt Golitko, an attorney for Tole, said in a statement released to The Athletic. “Our discussions have been productive, and we’re on a positive path toward an agreement that will allow the parties to move forward. Mr. Tole appreciates the progress we have achieved and looks forward to an amicable resolution.”

In another statement released Thursday, the Marion County Prosecutor’s Office said, “Our priority remains securing justice for Mr. Tole.”

The confrontation between Sanchez and Tole occurred early in the morning in downtown Indianapolis. Police said Sanchez was stabbed multiple times in his upper right torso, while Tole had a large laceration on his left cheek that also required hospitalization.

Sanchez was arrested and booked after being released from the hospital, and he told a local reporter as he left Marion County Jail at the time that he was “just focused on my recovery.”

“I just want to thank the first responders, Eskenazi Hospital,” Sanchez said, according to videos posted on social media by Fox59/CBS4. “I just want to thank Dr. (Lindsey) Mossler, the surgeon. She saved my life.”

Marion County Prosecutor Ryan Mears said at a news conference last October that the whole ordeal could have been avoided.

“We are literally talking about people fighting over a parking space or a dispute about where people are parking, and it resulted in someone receiving just incredibly significant injuries,” Mears said.

“Where this incident took place was an area of the city which was very well covered by surveillance footage. There are multiple angles of surveillance footage which capture the events that occurred. And in addition, we had a number of civilian witnesses who came forward (and) provided information about what took place.”
